## Current project: how cells hold an embryo together

*Postdoc, ISTA (Heisenberg group), since 2022 · funded by FWF ESPRIT and, before that, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND fellowship*

::: {.todo}
**DRAFT, please check and rewrite in your own words.** Keep to the research question. Don't describe unpublished results or show unpublished images (EM, segmentations, expression data) unless your PI has approved it.
:::

In the first hours of life, an embryo is just a handful of cells. Yet even at this stage it already has a precise, reproducible shape. I study how this happens in the embryo of the sea squirt *Phallusia* (an ascidian), a marine animal whose early embryos develop quickly and are beautifully transparent.

My work focuses on how cells stick to each other through adhesion molecules such as cadherins, and on how the network of contacts between cells shapes the embryo as a whole.

## PhD project: how tubes fuse

*PhD, University of Münster (Luschnig group), 2016–2021*

During my PhD I studied how the tubes of the fruit fly's breathing system (the trachea) connect to each other. I focused on membrane trafficking and cell mechanics during epithelial tube fusion.

Selected work from this period: a review on [how cells form tubes](../illustration/projects/2021-lumen-formation/index.qmd), with figures I made, a paper on tracheal tube fusion (*J Cell Sci*, 2022) and a co-first-author methods paper on [visualising membrane trafficking](../illustration/projects/2023-rush-trafficking-drosophila/index.qmd) (*Dev Cell*, 2023). See all [publications](publications.qmd).
